title: Nudging Farmers to Use Fertilizer: Theory and Experimental Evidence from Kenya
source_type: original field experiment and economic model
locator: AER 101(6), pp.2350–2390; inspected §III–IV, Tables 3–4, §VI and Table 6, particularly pp.2366–2377, 2383–2387.
scope_limit: Parents sampled through 16 Busia schools; household any-plot use is not purchaser-only use. Present bias is a proposed mechanism; welfare comparisons are model calibrations.
evidence_lineage: Original 2003–05 SAFI experiment and earlier pilots with ICS; related Busia agronomic trials in S02. Programme population and team overlap; not independent replication.

title: How High Are Rates of Return to Fertilizer? Evidence from Field Experiments in Kenya
locator: AER Papers and Proceedings 98(2), pp.482–488; entire short paper, especially research design and Tables 1–2.
scope_limit: Research-assisted small plots and calculated net returns, not nationwide expected profits. Dose, labour assumptions and stochastic yields matter.
evidence_lineage: Six on-farm experimental seasons beginning July 2000 in Busia; original plot measurements. Related research programme to S01, with some prior-participant pilots carried forward.

title: Learning Through Noticing: Theory and Evidence from a Field Experiment
source_type: original field experiment and learning model
locator: QJE 129(3), pp.1311–1353; §III, Tables II–V, §IV.C, footnotes 23–29; pp.1325–1342.
scope_limit: 489 experienced farmers from seven Indonesian villages; 117 trial participants; short follow-up. Trial then explanation are sequential, not separate randomisations.
evidence_lineage: Original 2006 census and 2007–08 seaweed surveys, plot trials and enumerator measures. September 2012 NBER draft also downloaded but final 2014 version used; those versions are one evidence lineage.

title: Can Network Theory-based Targeting Increase Technology Adoption? (January 2021 author manuscript)
source_type: original cluster field experiment; author manuscript
locator: January 2021 manuscript, §§2–5 and Appendix A; pp.5–15, results tables and mechanism discussion; published AER DOI 10.1257/aer.20200295.
scope_limit: Manuscript inspected, not publisher typeset edition. Three semi-arid districts; 2–3 observed seasons. Centrality is changed with selection, and exact contagion process remains underdetermined.
evidence_lineage: Original 200-village network census and 2011–13 household surveys; same research network and extension partner as S05–S06, but separate experimental design. Community overlap across trials was not independently crosschecked.

title: Social Learning and Incentives for Experimentation and Communication
locator: Public copyedited advance-2018 version, Review of Economic Studies, DOI 10.1093/restud/rdy039; §§2,4–8, Tables 1–2 and 5–7; pp.4–8, outcomes and labour analysis.
scope_limit: 120-village analytic experiment; one lead farmer versus five peers confounds communicator identity and number. Distinguish pit planting and crop-residue management.
evidence_lineage: Original Malawi 2009–11 extension experiment; overlapping cross-cutting assignments and some shared observations with S06. Gender-reserved villages excluded from this paper’s analytic subset; S06 §2.7 states this explicitly.

title: Gender Gaps in Technology Diffusion (public author manuscript)
source_type: original cluster field experiment; author manuscript
locator: Author manuscript available at October 2019 path; §§2.7,3,4,5; Tables 3–7, especially pp.11–21. Later published in Journal of Development Economics.
scope_limit: Female-reserved versus unreserved communicator roles, not randomly assigning sex to otherwise identical people. Perceptions measured independently of uptake; pooled adoption/yield gaps imprecise and female-recipient subgroup gaps remain.
evidence_lineage: Original 143-village Malawi 2009–11 data; same larger experiment as S05, with overlapping unreserved villages and different analytic samples. Cross-cutting treatment interactions not powered.

title: The Effects of Service-Delivery Model and Purchase Price on Hearing-Aid Outcomes in Older Adults: A Randomized Double-Blind Placebo-Controlled Clinical Trial
source_type: original randomised clinical trial with nonrandom price cohorts
locator: Methods: trial design, participants, outcome measures; Results: service delivery, maintenance, decision to keep and extension; Figures 6–10, 12–14 and Table 5.
scope_limit: 163 volunteers, 154 completers; mostly White, educated and relatively affluent, no prior hearing aid use. Service assignment randomised; prices sequential. Post-trial fitting extension not an independently randomised contrast. Apply S13 correction.
evidence_lineage: Original Indiana University single-site trial, 2 November 2012–31 August 2016; same participants for benefits, satisfaction, datalogged use and returns. S13 corrects its speech-test calibration; it is not independent corroboration.

title: Differences Between Older Adults Who Do and Do Not Try Hearing Aids and Between Those Who Keep and Return the Devices
source_type: original observational analysis of research volunteers
locator: Methods: Participants (2004–08 recruitment); Results: adherents/nonadherents and keep/return comparisons; Tables and Discussion.
scope_limit: 139 first-time-user analytic participants selected from a larger recruitment pool; only 34 nonpurchasers completed comparison measures. Associations adjusted for hearing loss are not randomised belief effects.
evidence_lineage: Reanalysis of original Indiana 2004–08 hearing-aid outcome study, parts reported in 2009/2010. Different cohort from S07; those earlier reports were not separately inspected.

title: The Stigma of Hearing Loss
locator: Methods; Results themes: altered self-perception, ageism, vanity, supportive/nonsupportive others; contrary cases and Discussion.
scope_limit: 91 help-seeking Bay Area dyads, 90% White hearing-impaired participants; nonrepresentative. Interviews elicit meanings and attributed reasons; they do not identify a population causal effect of stigma. Field dates not specified in inspected text.
evidence_lineage: Original separately conducted interviews with each dyad member at baseline, three and twelve months (91,87,84 dyads). Marketing and laboratory sources cited by this paper were not independently inspected or adopted as empirical findings.

title: Cycling to School: Increasing Secondary School Enrollment for Girls in India
locator: AEJ Applied Economics 9(3), pp.321–350; programme §I; data/design §§II–III; Table 2, distance analysis, Table 8 placebo; pp.326–345.
scope_limit: Bihar programme exposure, age-appropriate grade-9 enrolment/completion, not individual riding or broad lifetime education. Triple difference depends on trends; norms and safety channels not separately identified.
evidence_lineage: Original analysis of DLHS-3 2007–08, earlier school enrolment records and exam records. Implementation/leakage evidence in Ghatak et al. is inherited here, not an independently inspected record. S12 reuses this policy and main survey lineage.

title: Wheels of Change: Transforming Girls’ Lives with Bicycles (7 May 2025 author manuscript)
source_type: original cluster field experiment; author manuscript
locator: 7 May 2025 manuscript, §§3–6 and Appendix B; Tables 1–6, A.4 and A.11; pp.8–24,38–43,56,74–75.
scope_limit: 100 public basic schools in three Zambian districts; initially enrolled grade5–7 girls walking >3km. Urban and some very remote schools excluded; disability/cycling-ability representation and route accessibility not established. Survey attrition differs across arms; later administrative outcomes not preregistered. Pooled aspirations imprecise in Tables3/A.11, despite positive wording in the manuscript and final S14 abstracts. Final tables/definitions not inspected; discrepancy unresolved.
evidence_lineage: Original 2017–18 trial survey plus 2019–21 administrative follow-up collected with implementing partner WBR; 2022 draft preserved separately. Same evidence lineage as final article S14. Programme includes mechanics, monitoring and use restrictions; not a bare bicycle transfer.

title: Infrastructure and Girls’ Education: Bicycles, Roads, and the Gender Education Gap in India
locator: ifo Working Paper 382, November 2022; §§2–4, road-variable construction pp.4–5, identification cautions pp.9–10, Tables 3–4.
scope_limit: All-weather road to health facilities proxies road access to school; missing road indicator does not mean no road. Road access not randomised. Null coefficient outside connected villages cannot establish strict necessity.
evidence_lineage: Reuses Bihar bicycle programme and DLHS-3 2007–08 central to S10; adds DLHS-2 pretrend evidence and road heterogeneity. Not an independent policy replication.

title: Erratum: Hearing-aid clinical trials and Connected Speech Test calibration
authors: American Speech-Language-Hearing Association; correction to Humes et al.
locator: American Journal of Audiology 28(3):730, DOI 10.1044/2019_AJA-19-0087; full correction.
scope_limit: Corrects signal-to-noise ratio from +3 to +1 dB. Authors expect relative benefit to be little affected, but this was not independently recomputed.
evidence_lineage: Correction to S07 and Humes et al. 2019 follow-up (latter not included as a separately analysed study). Same underlying tests; no independent replication.

title: Wheels of Change: Transforming Girls’ Lives with Bicycles (final journal abstract and metadata)
locator: Economic Journal 136(679), October 2026, pp.2531–2561; online publication 8 November 2025; abstract and publication metadata.
scope_limit: Final full text not acquired. Abstract reports rounded34% commute/29% absenteeism reductions and says educational aspirations improved. That aspirations wording differs from S11 pooled Tables3/A.11:0.07(SE0.05) and0.06 with corrected p=.44/.50. Final tables, definitions and pooled/arm-specific interpretation remain unverified; do not infer a changed published estimate or a positive pooled effect.
evidence_lineage: Final publication of same Zambia trial as S11, not independent evidence. Commute/absence rounding accords with S11 tables, whereas its opening abstract retained older35%/27% values. The aspirations narrative/table difference is unresolved, not explained by rounding.
